subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When a spit grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it, it forms a:
questions.explain: A bar forms where a spit extends across a bay, often enclosing a lagoon.

questions.q: A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a:
questions.explain: A spit is a depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end, formed by longshore drift.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the correct order in which erosional landforms develop on a headland?
questions.explain: A crack becomes a cave, then an arch, then a stack when the arch collapses, then a stump.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is an example of:
questions.explain: Beach nourishment, adding sand or shingle, is a soft engineering approach.

questions.q: Constructive waves are best described as:
options: Waves that only occur in storms
Low, gentle waves with a strong swash that build up beaches
High, frequent waves with a strong backwash that erode beaches
Waves that flow inland as rivers
questions.explain: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, depositing material to build beaches.

options: Allowing low-value land to flood and the coastline to move back
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating natural defences like salt marsh.

questions.q: A flood hydrograph with a short lag time and high peak discharge usually indicates:
options: A rapid flashy response, e.g. urban or impermeable basin
A gentle slow response, e.g. forested basin
questions.explain: A short lag time and high peak show water reaching the river quickly, raising flood risk.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is the:
questions.explain: A drainage basin is the whole area of land drained by a river system.

questions.q: Dissolved minerals carried invisibly in the water are transported by:
questions.explain: In solution, dissolved load is carried chemically within the water.
